newsitem.title: USA: Tropical storm Ana heads away from U.S. coast.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm Ana heads away from U.S. coast.

text.p: Tropical Storm Ana spun northeast across the Atlantic Ocean Thursday, but posed no threat to Bermuda as it made its way to cooler waters, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said.
At 11:00 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), Tropical Storm Ana's center was near latitude 35.5 north and longitude 68.4 west, or about 415 miles east of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina.
The storm, moving northeast at near 10 mph (16 kph), was expected to accelerate and lose its tropical characteristics over the next day or so, forecasters said.
Maximum sustained winds were near 40 mph (64 kph), making Ana only a minimal tropical storm.
Ana is the first tropical storm of the June-November Atlantic hurricane season.
